textbookBox.concept: The traffic police write to children who reach school on foot, by bicycle or by bus. Roads are often busy with traffic and at times dangerous, so the police want to share tips to cross and walk

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: The traffic police write to children who reach school on foot, by bicycle or by bus. Roads are often busy with traffic and at times dangerous, so the police want to share tips to cross and walk safely.
beats.speakEn: The traffic police write to children who reach school on foot, by bicycle or by bus. Roads are often busy with traffic and at times dangerous, so the police want to share tips to cross and walk safely.

beats.en: Rule 1: always use the zebra crossing, the black and white stripes on the road. Look right, then left, then right again, and cross only when it is safe. Rule 2: follow traffic lights.
beats.speakEn: Rule 1: always use the zebra crossing, the black and white stripes on the road. Look right, then left, then right again, and cross only when it is safe. Rule 2: follow traffic lights.

type: Key Concept: The traffic police write to children who reach school on foot, by bicycle or by bus.
Rule: Rule 1: always use the zebra crossing, the black and white stripes on the road.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 4 english · Be Smart, Be Safe · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: Rule 4: hold an adult's hand when you walk near the road, especially while crossing. Rule 5: use reflective stickers if you walk in the evening, so drivers can see you clearly in the dark.

beats.en: Rule 4: hold an adult's hand when you walk near the road, especially while crossing. Rule 5: use reflective stickers if you walk in the evening, so drivers can see you clearly in the dark. Rule 6: be alert.
beats.speakEn: Rule 4: hold an adult's hand when you walk near the road, especially while crossing. Rule 5: use reflective stickers if you walk in the evening, so drivers can see you clearly in the dark. Rule 6: be alert.

beats.en: A pedestrian is a person who walks on the road or footpath. A footpath is the part of the road kept for people to walk on. Reflective things shine back light so they can be seen in the dark.
beats.speakEn: A pedestrian is a person who walks on the road or footpath. A footpath is the part of the road kept for people to walk on. Reflective things shine back light so they can be seen in the dark.

type: Rule 4: hold an adult's hand when you walk near the road, especially while crossing.
A pedestrian is a person who walks on the road or footpath.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 4 english · Be Smart, Be Safe · Complete Summary
textbookBox.concept: Signs on the road give us messages without words. Some tell us what to do and some tell us what not to do. School ahead warns drivers to slow down. No honking means do not blow the horn.

beats.en: Let us review the key takeaway from Be Smart, Be Safe: Signs on the road give us messages without words. Some tell us what to do and some tell us what not to do. School ahead warns drivers to slow down. No honking means do not blow the horn.
